programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: Tha Fuigheag a’ feuchainn ris a h-uile càil 's urrainn dha ith'. Tha e gu math doirbh baga-lòin a phacadh nuair tha Fuigheag faisg air làimh. Fuigheag is trying to eat everything he can. It’s very difficult to pack a lunchbag when Fuigheag is nearby.

programme.title: Lon le Linda
programme.desc: Tha Linda NicLeòid a’ còcaireachd cuide ri a caraidean. An-diugh tha Rowan agus Calum Fraser cuide rithe agus iad a’ deasachadh risotto le feòil-circe agus piobar dearg. Ach mus tòisich iad a’ còcaireachd, feumaidh iad dèanamh cinnteach gu bheil na tha a dhìth orra a-staigh. Mur a bheil, nì iad liosta agus thèid iad dhan bhùth airson a h-uile càil fhaighinn. Bidh Linda agus a caraidean cuideachd a’ faighinn a-mach cò às a tha peasairean a’ tighinn. Tha iad an uairsin a’ tilleadh dhan chidsin airson an risotto a dhèanamh mus suidh iad sìos aig a’ bhòrd ga ithe! Linda is joined by Rowan and Calum Fraser to make a delicious risotto with chicken and red peppers. But first they must ensure they have all the ingredients and, if not, they make a list and go shopping. They also learn more about where peas come from, and then it’s back to the kitchen to prepare the risotto before sitting down to eat!

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Tha Àtaidh a’ cur èisg ghleansach ris a’ chruinneachadh aige, ach chan fhada gus an tuig e gu bheil iad a’ toirt suas barrachd rùm na bha e an dùil. Nise càit’ an cadail e? Abney adds some shiny fish to his collection but soon finds that they take up more room than expected. Now where can he get some sleep?

programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc: Tha iad uile a’ cruinneachadh san Achadh Fhiadhaich an-diugh airson òran mòr grinn a thoirt dhuin. Everyone is gathering in Achadh Fhiadhaich today to sing a big, lovely song.

programme.title: Dan & Gran
programme.desc: Stan and Gran get the giggles while spotting nature on the Ley, and the lake seems to be giggling back at them! Who is that laughing? Tha Dan is Gran a' cireasail fhad 's a tha 'd a' coimhead nàdar air an Loch, 's tha 'n Loch mar gu bheil e a' cireasail air ais thuca! Cò tha siud a' gàireachdaich?

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Patsi NicCoinnich a’ leughadh An Nighean Nach Do Rinn Mearachd A-riamh. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Mark Pett agus Gary Rubenstein agus a dhealbhachadh le Mark Pett. Chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Jo NicDhòmhnaill. A bedtime story for young children. Patsi Mackenzie reads An Nighean Nach Do Rinn Mearachd A-riamh, written by Mark Pett and Gary Rubenstein, illustrated by Mark Pett and translated into Gaelic by Jo Macdonald.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Sombaidh Ceitidh a’ gabhail fear de shiùcairean Granaidh, is tha bhlas cho làidir is gu bheil e a’ cur a h-anam beò aiste. Feumaidh Pòl is a charaidean feuchainn ri h-anam beò a thilleadh air ais na bodhaig, mus bheil e ro anmoch. Zombie Katie is so shocked by the taste of one of Gran’s Fishermen’s Enemy sweets that her life force leaves her body. Dave and his friends need to find Katie’s naughty life force before it is too late.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Gun fhiosta dha, tha Pòl a’ dèanamh toll ann am fànas agus feumaidh e feuchainn ri dòigh fhaighinn air a chàradh mus tèid gach nì a tharraing a-steach dhan toll mhòr dhubh. Dave accidentally rips the fabric of space and must find a way to fix it before the whole universe gets sucked inside the black hole beyond.

programme.title: Hilda
programme.desc: Nuair a tha bacadh air Hilda, tha i a' cur sùim na nàbaidh, Mgr Ostenfeld. Tha i ri lorg iris a tha caogad bliadhn’ a dh’aois 's, ri linn sin, tha i fhèin is Artair a' siùbhal tro thìm, air turas do-chreidsinneach. When Hilda is grounded, she takes an interest in her neighbour, Mr Ostenfeld. She finds a 50-year old magazine and, as a result, she and Artair travel through time on an unbelievable trip.

programme.title: Na Speuran
programme.desc: Thèid air turas suas dha na speuran cuide ris an Speuradair Bekah! Air an turas fànais iongantach seo tha i ag innse dhuinn mar a thàinig a’ ghealach gu bith. Blast off into space with Astronaut Bekah! In this amazing space voyage, she tells us how the moon came into existence.

programme.title: Gàrraidhean Mòra
programme.desc: Mairi Rodgers explores Falkland Palace Garden in Fife. Tha Màiri Rodgers a’ gabhail cuairt tro Ghàrradh Lùchairt Falkland.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Learner Emily MacDonald chats to Joy in the studio and Calum Maclean takes a wheeled adventure, charting the part Scotland played in the development of the bicycle.

programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Suas gu Deas
programme.desc: Tha aifreann nan iasgair ann am Barraigh agus show Uibhist a Tuath ann a Homhstadh. The fisherman’s mass is held on Castlebay pier and it’s a busy day at the North Uist show.

programme.title: Cocain is na Klondykers

programme.title: Cùram

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc: Lucy visits a favourite east coast location to show Mary Ann seabuckthorn, which grows in shoreline dunes.

programme.title: Machair
programme.desc: Drama Gàidhlig stèidhichte ann an Leòdhas. Gaelic soap based on the Isle of Lewis.

programme.title: Fraochy Bay
programme.desc: Fàilte gu Fraochy Bay , baile nach fhaic thu a h-uile là! Is iomadh annas a tha ri fhaicinn sa bhaile , agus sin gun ghuth air cail ach muinntir a bhaile fhèin. Tha P.C. MacIlleathain air a sharachadh le obair paipeir ach eil sgeul air trusdair a nith cobhair air? Welcome to the colourful and unusual world of Fraochy Bay, a miniature metropolis somewhere off the fringes of the map. Officer MacLean is disappearing under a pile of paperwork, dreaming of fast car pursuits and major crime busts. Is something finally about to happen?

programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Sreath spioradail le laoidhean, sailm agus leughaidhean. A series of spiritual music, reflections and readings.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Quiz show presented by Victoria Coren in which knowledge will only take you so far, as patience and lateral thinking are also vital. Three maths graduates take on a team featuring a linguistics graduate, an English graduate and an IT developer who is also a proofreader. They compete to draw together the connections between things which, at first glance, seem utterly random, from 'drip dry' to 'equal by definition' to 'MPs' obligation to vote' to 'exit 300yds ahead'.

programme.title: American Visions

programme.title: Only Connect

programme.title: Artsnight
programme.desc: Carla Lane redefined British comedy drama in the 1970s with her unique brand of 'situation tragedy'. At a time when television writing was the preserve of middle-class men, she brought a convincing cast of working-class female characters to British screens. The daring honesty with which she told the stories of ordinary women revolutionised the roles available to actresses on TV and blazed a trail for the screenwriters following in her footsteps. This special edition of Artsnight delves into the BBC's archive and brings together rarely seen interviews in which writer Carla Lane discusses her life and work, while Carla's son Carl offers personal insights into his mother's career and legacy. With contributions from the Liver Birds - Polly James and Nerys Hughes - and Geoffrey Palmer, the long-suffering husband to Ria in Butterflies.

programme.title: Butterflies
programme.desc: Ria has enough to cope with: there is her husband Ben, who has his own hang-ups and her sons Adam and Russell, who are the cause of most of them. Then suddenly there's Leonard.

programme.title: A History of Britain by Simon Schama
programme.desc: She began the century that bears her name a princess and ended it as an empress. Queen Victoria ruled one of the most powerful empires in world history during a century of staggering change - for both good and bad. But it was Victorian women who were at the forefront of the fight against its excesses and inequalities, who campaigned for the rights for ordinary people in marriage, education, medicine and the vote.

programme.title: Muhammad Ali
programme.desc: Born in Louisville, Kentucky in 1942, Cassius Clay rises from the world of amateur boxing to win gold at the 1960 Olympic Games. Following his Olympic success, Clay turns professional and moves to Miami to train with Angelo Dundee, sharpening his boxing skills and honing his genius for self-promotion.

programme.title: Muhammad Ali
programme.desc: Cassius Clay is determined to become the youngest ever champion by taking on the ‘unbeatable’ Sonny Liston, the reigning world heavyweight champion. Clay needs to fight other contenders first, including a famous bout with Henry Cooper in London. Meanwhile, he quietly joins the Nation of Islam and becomes a confidant of Malcolm X.

programme.title: Muhammad Ali
programme.desc: Cassius Clay publicly joins the Nation of Islam and adopts the name Muhammad Ali. For three years, he dominates the heavyweight ranks, but in 1967 the US army extends the military draft, and Ali becomes eligible for service in Vietnam.

programme.title: Muhammad Ali
programme.desc: Muhammad Ali refuses induction into the US Army as a conscientious objector and becomes one of the most reviled men in America. Ali, stripped of his title, is convicted of draft evasion and forced into exile. In 1970, he triumphantly returns to the ring, but it’s clear that he has lost a step.

programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: Will the Iran war cut Europe’s dependence on energy imports? Soaring energy prices are hurting businesses and household budgets across Europe, so will this crisis change the continent's energy mix for good? Despite efforts to switch to renewables, Europe is still hugely reliant on imported oil and gas. The CEO of Europe’s biggest gas distributor, Italgas, Paolo Gallo explains how new technology can help and Ben Thompson also hears from EU energy commissioner Dan Jørgensen about concerns that moving to solar, wind and nuclear power could just shift Europe’s dependency to other parts of the world.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: In glorious Gloucestershire, Nicki Chapman helps Peggy finally make her long-awaited escape from London. After years of dreaming, she’s ready to find a home that suits her and her crew – two dogs and a horse called Tom. Emotions are running high as Nicki lines up a selection of spectacular properties from where some of the county’s amazing views can be seen. Nicki also meets a pair of street food chefs who have swapped the city buzz for a slice of country living.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris and Amelia are in Barnsley to transform Rea and her daughter India’s bland and unsafe patch into a boho-style garden influenced by their love of upcycling, crafting and all things rustic. India would love a fairy area, while mum Rea wants a space to relax in and socialise with friends. Can the team achieve all this on a £5,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Mohsin, Gus, Amir and Ayoub – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Mohsin, Gus, Amir and Ayoub – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek gets some northern nostalgia as he remembers three of his best walks in north Wales. Cadair Idris is a mountain steeped in legend and mythology - it's also one of Wales's most spectacular summits. Derek climbs to three peaks in this range and even braves an icy cold dip in its glacial lake, where the temperature, quite literally, takes his breath away. The second walk Derek recalls is from the Italianate village of Portmeirion, where he also discovers Y Gwyllt - ‘the wild’ headland beyond. Finally, Derek walks the Dee Valley Way, a stunning 13-mile route which takes him from the pretty town of Corwen to its larger and more bustling neighbour, Llangollen. On the walk, he learns of a warrior prince and leads a horse-drawn barge along the Llangollen canal.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: In glorious Gloucestershire, Nicki Chapman helps Peggy finally make her long-awaited escape from London. After years of dreaming, she’s ready to find a home that suits her and her crew – two dogs and a horse called Tom. Emotions are running high as Nicki lines up a selection of spectacular properties from where some of the county’s amazing views can be seen. Nicki also meets a pair of street food chefs who have swapped the city buzz for a slice of country living.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris and Amelia are in Barnsley to transform Rea and her daughter India’s bland and unsafe patch into a boho-style garden influenced by their love of upcycling, crafting and all things rustic. India would love a fairy area, while mum Rea wants a space to relax in and socialise with friends. Can the team achieve all this on a £5,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Mohsin, Gus, Amir and Ayoub – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Brickies
programme.desc: In this episode, three groups of brickies are on a housing development in Stoke-on-Trent. The brickies are under pressure to get the job done, but with a national shortage of materials, nothing is guaranteed. Jeorgia, from Wales, hopes to realise her dream of buying a sporty new car, but is dealing with the stress of working away from her home and family for the first time in her life. The site’s newest apprentice, Tom T, hopes to prove himself as he gets to grips with life in the real working world. And things take a turn for Tom C - the site’s labourer - when he unexpectedly finds himself out of a home and searching for somewhere to live.

programme.title: Brickies
programme.desc: The brickies are back in Stoke-on-Trent where things are falling behind schedule and a national mortar shortage threatens to grind production to a halt. Local bricklayer Patch has been drafted in to give the build an extra push. A young father of two, Patch has earmarked a forthcoming family holiday for the moment he hopes to finally ‘pop the question’ to his long-term girlfriend. After a falling-out at home, labourer Tom C is still searching for somewhere to stay. His workmates are there for him as he works through his options. He arranges to meet his ex- girlfriend as he looks to get things back on track. Meanwhile, after years of building homes for other people, Kuda is finally ready to buy his first dream house.

programme.title: Brickies
programme.desc: Newcomer Molly is used to working on smaller private jobs, but she’s now hitting the big time on a new housing development in Northampton. Describing herself as 'the only brickie you'll ever meet with hair extensions and fake eyelashes', she's larger than life. It’s the battle of the apprentices as the site’s young brickies, Lucas and Zac, go head-to-head and trade insults. Their rivalry begins at work but is settled on the foot golf pitch. Hard-working Kuda is hoping to hear back on his mission to buy his first house. The big boss visits the site and brings news - but it’s not what Kuda is expecting.

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: Jobless is a sitcom all about the Adenugas, a middle-class British Nigerian family in Milton Keynes, in particular 16-year-old twin brother and sister Kehinde and Taiwo. Kenny is the family joker, who dreams of fame and fortune; sister Tai is, by contrast, sarcastic, super-smart and anxious to prove it. The twins live at home with their parents. Their mum, Bunmi, (chatty, energetic, control-freak tendencies, has a very stern side) runs Bunmi’s Beauty Salon, and despairs at her hapless offspring and their schemes to hit the big time. Tai and Kenny are desperate to make money by any means necessary – not only is financial independence very alluring, but the pressure they face from Bunmi doesn’t help. The twins’ different personalities inform their different approaches, however it seems neither of those personalities are quite compatible with the world of work.

programme.title: Match of the Day Wales
programme.desc: Live international football as Wales welcome World Cup-bound Ghana to the Cardiff City Stadium.

programme.title: Louis Theroux
programme.desc: Louis reflects on the criminal justice system in the USA, which has more prisoners than any other country in the world. In documentaries such as Behind Bars and Miami Mega Jail, Louis spent time with hundreds of incarcerated men, discovering a world with its own rules and codes and a system that seemed to be broken. In A Place for Paedophiles, Louis came face to face with those responsible for serious sex crimes against children who were being locked up indefinitely, even after their sentences had been completed. Louis also revisits his documentaries in Philadelphia and Milwaukee, where tensions between the African-American community and the police were already at boiling point, years before the recent killing of George Floyd.

programme.title: Fake Friend: The Ticket Scammer
programme.desc: How a Somerset high-flyer turned his charm and connections into tools of deception – conning his school friends and hundreds of others while living a life of glamour himself.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond, James May and the Stig return. Jeremy asks why there aren't more three-wheeled cars in the world and investigates further with a closer look at the 1980s comedians' favourite, the Reliant Robin. Meanwhile, James gives Top Gear's favourite warhorse, the Toyota Hilux pick up, one final assignment as he attempts to drive one up an active volcano in Iceland and the Stig rips up the track in the new Bentley Continental Supersports. Plus, Richard gives the old Chevrolet Lacetti a dignified send-off before he and Clarkson host a star-studded tea party to welcome in a shiny new Reasonably Priced Car.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: Springwatch returns for three weeks of seasonal splendour. Broadcasting live from the brand new location of National Trust Crom in Northern Ireland, Chris Packham and Michaela Strachan deliver all the wildlife drama spring has to offer. With remote cameras rigged across the site, they uncover stories unfolding in real time. Iolo Williams undertakes his own wildlife wanderings, broadcasting live from the Knepp Estate in Sussex, where wildlife is thriving and ‘stand-out’ species are returning to the landscape.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: A hundred years ago in Yorkshire, it wasn’t ketchup that people added to their food - it was a delicious locally made relish. By the turn of the 20th century, 30 million bottles of Yorkshire Relish were being made in Leeds each year and shipped around the world. Made of vinegar, sugar, fruits and 27 spices, it was the go-to sauce for generations, right up until the 1950s. In the city where it was made, Danny Sebastian savours a collection of advertising items that celebrate this once-popular condiment. If that doesn’t whet your appetite, enjoy two teams of bargain hunters as they scour the antiques stalls at Wetherby Racecourse. On the red team are twins and classic car fans Mike and Joe, who hope to breakdance their way to victory - as long as they don’t break the bank first! Against them are mum and daughter Sue and Sarah, who plan on using their cha-cha-charm to get a good price. But which team will be dancing all the way to a profit at Caroline Hawley’s auction?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: On the last leg of his journey, Michael Portillo arrives in the historic northern city of Eger. At its famous castle, he discovers how, during the 16th century, Ottoman invaders were defeated by a vastly outnumbered Hungarian force. It‘s a victory still celebrated to this day. Nearby, in the foothills of the Bükk Mountains, one of Hungary’s wine-producing areas, Michael takes a tour of a family-owned vineyard and samples the region’s signature wine, Bull’s Blood. Continuing east, his final destination is the Puszta, Hungary's largest national park, where animals have grazed for over 2,000 years. On a vast plain with endless skies, Michael is treated to an impressive display of horsemanship by Hungarian cowboys, called csikós.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Leicestershire, Brandy, an elderly horse, is trapped in freezing mud on the banks of the Ashby canal. As the exhausted animal weakens, farmers and a specialist fire and rescue team join forces in a race against the clock to save him. With age and size working against him, the team make one final, desperate attempt to bring Brandy to safety, before it’s too late. In Lincolnshire, arson rips through a family farm, destroying buildings, animal enclosures and years of hard work. As the owners count the cost of the devastation, another farmer in Scotland recounts her own ordeal - watching her only tractor explode into flames after a petrol bomb attack. With deliberate farm fires on the rise, experts reveal how even a single act of recklessness can cause hundreds of thousands of pounds in damage. And in Hampshire, reporter Paul Colgan meets the innovators using drones to deliver defibrillators to the most remote corners of the countryside. By slashing emergency response times, this cutting-edge technology could transform the chances of survival and save lives on farms and in rural communities across the UK.

programme.title: Lost and Found in the Lakes
programme.desc: The detectorists join forces with the freedivers to find not one but two family heirlooms lost by a heartbroken daughter. Glass artist Peter turns old, thrown-away bottles into stained-glass beauty, and archaeologist Sam looks into what could be our oldest find by our youngest treasure hunter.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: The quiz show where players must avoid Impossible answers to stay in the competition. 20 people start today’s show, but how many of them will survive to face the £10,000 question?

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: The hunt for the nation's Mastermind continues as Clive Myrie tests four more contenders on their specialist subjects and general knowledge under the glare of the spotlight and the ticking clock. The subjects in this episode are Marcus Trescothick, Rupert Brooke, Thomas Cromwell and the films of Wes Anderson.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: Jan has lived in her three-bedroom house for over 30 years, but working seven days a week leaves her little time to clean and organise, and her collection of clothes and shoes are covered in dust. The team has just one day to turn her bedroom into a relaxing sanctuary and give her space to rediscover her love of fashion.

programme.title: The Great British Countryside
programme.desc: Hugh Dennis and Julia Bradbury venture across Britain's biggest county, Yorkshire, from the Moors and the Dales to the coast to discover how Britain's epic past lives on in the most fascinating stories and characters. Hugh takes the controls of a glider, and gets winched down into one of Britain's largest potholes on the end of a rope, past the tallest unbroken waterfall in Britain. Julia finds out how Yorkshire's rocks have turned Agatha Christie's handbag to stone, and how they produce mineral water. For a country the size of Britain, it has the biggest variety of geology on Earth, which has created not only a beautiful landscape, but also a fascinating industrial heritage, a rich history and many legends.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel presents the show in which members of the public are invited to bring along their antiques for examination. This edition from Ramsgate in Kent features two teddy bears with their own x-ray plates from a dentist, a penny with a date which makes it worth a small fortune, a handbag made from an armadillo shell, and a valuable collection of Louis Wain cat pictures.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from the historic Blackpool Tower Circus. Paul Martin is joined by experts Anita Manning and James Lewis. Together the team pick out a selection of interesting antiques and collectibles to be sold at a local auction. James discovers some terracotta tomb figures that could be over 1,000 years old, and Anita gets her hands on a collection of seaside postcards. But the real star of the show is a well-preserved concertina. Paul also takes a look at one of Lancashire's most famous theatres, the Morecambe Winter Gardens, and tries his hand at some watercolour painting with renowned artist Geoff Butterworth.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Nikki Fox, Ruthie Henshall, Danny John-Jules and Ignacio Lopez take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s Belgian rail journey continues in the Dutch speaking region of Flanders. In Antwerp, he discovers the city's historic multibillion-pound diamond industry and drops in at the workshop of an expert. Just outside the city, Michael boards the Dendermonde to Puurs Heritage Railway, run by volunteers, and gets a chance to drive one of its 1950s diesel engines. Heading to Belgium’s third city, Ghent, Michael visits the magnificent cathedral and marvels at a 15th-century Van Eyck masterpiece, the Adoration of the Mystic Lamb, the most stolen painting in the world.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing Simply Provence
programme.desc: It’s fair to say that when it comes to classic national dishes, the French and British like to do things differently. However, both have a passion for poisson. Forty-five per cent of French households eat fish at least once a week, and Marcus wants to find out what kind of fish they like and if there’s a French dish to rival the great British fish and chips. If there's one fruit that might be even more synonymous with Provence than garlic, it's the olive. They’ve been grown here for over 3,500 years, and Marcus wants to understand the region’s passion for these tiny, versatile delights.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham and Michaela Strachan present the latest seasonal wildlife stories live from National Trust Crom, the stunning lakeside reserve cared for by the National Trust. Featuring part one of a special trilogy of short films examining the extraordinary relationship between the reed warbler and the common cuckoo, one of nature’s most fascinating examples of brood parasitism. Meanwhile, Iolo Williams broadcasts live from the Natural History Museum in London, where he turns the spotlight on the capital’s rich and often-overlooked invertebrate life.

programme.title: QI XL
programme.desc: Let Sandi Toksvig bring you to your senses with Aisling Bea, Roisin Conaty, Jessica Fostekew and Alan Davies.

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: The brilliant Ardal O’Hanlon introduces to the stage the amazing Mawaan Rizwan and the hilarious Sara Barron.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Matt Chorley.

programme.title: The Road to Hope with Fergal Keane
programme.desc: The BBC’s Fergal Keane has spent 40 years witnessing the worst that humanity can do - genocide, war, and famine. So why is he full of hope? The answer lies in the extraordinary bravery he’s encountered in the worst places. In this powerful and humane film by Oscar-winner Alice Doyard, Fergal argues that despite the anxiety of the present we have real cause for hope.

programme.title: Defiance
programme.desc: Thriller based on a true story. In 1940s eastern Europe, four Jewish brothers flee to the forest to escape persecution and death at the hands of Nazi forces after their parents are murdered. Once there, they find more refugees are using the forest as a hideout, so they band together to share resources and attempt to outwit the German forces, who are always on their tail.

programme.title: Race Across the World
programme.desc: Six months after the race, all five teams reunite to relive their 12,000km journey from Palermo to Mongolia, with unseen moments and unprecedented behind-the-scenes access

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: Springwatch returns for three weeks of seasonal splendour. Broadcasting live from the brand new location of National Trust Crom in Northern Ireland, Chris Packham and Michaela Strachan deliver all the wildlife drama spring has to offer. With remote cameras rigged across the site, they uncover stories unfolding in real time. Iolo Williams undertakes his own wildlife wanderings, broadcasting live from the Knepp Estate in Sussex, where wildlife is thriving and ‘stand-out’ species are returning to the landscape.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: A hundred years ago in Yorkshire, it wasn’t ketchup that people added to their food - it was a delicious locally made relish. By the turn of the 20th century, 30 million bottles of Yorkshire Relish were being made in Leeds each year and shipped around the world. Made of vinegar, sugar, fruits and 27 spices, it was the go-to sauce for generations, right up until the 1950s. In the city where it was made, Danny Sebastian savours a collection of advertising items that celebrate this once-popular condiment. If that doesn’t whet your appetite, enjoy two teams of bargain hunters as they scour the antiques stalls at Wetherby Racecourse. On the red team are twins and classic car fans Mike and Joe, who hope to breakdance their way to victory - as long as they don’t break the bank first! Against them are mum and daughter Sue and Sarah, who plan on using their cha-cha-charm to get a good price. But which team will be dancing all the way to a profit at Caroline Hawley’s auction?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: On the last leg of his journey, Michael Portillo arrives in the historic northern city of Eger. At its famous castle, he discovers how, during the 16th century, Ottoman invaders were defeated by a vastly outnumbered Hungarian force. It‘s a victory still celebrated to this day. Nearby, in the foothills of the Bükk Mountains, one of Hungary’s wine-producing areas, Michael takes a tour of a family-owned vineyard and samples the region’s signature wine, Bull’s Blood. Continuing east, his final destination is the Puszta, Hungary's largest national park, where animals have grazed for over 2,000 years. On a vast plain with endless skies, Michael is treated to an impressive display of horsemanship by Hungarian cowboys, called csikós.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Leicestershire, Brandy, an elderly horse, is trapped in freezing mud on the banks of the Ashby canal. As the exhausted animal weakens, farmers and a specialist fire and rescue team join forces in a race against the clock to save him. With age and size working against him, the team make one final, desperate attempt to bring Brandy to safety, before it’s too late. In Lincolnshire, arson rips through a family farm, destroying buildings, animal enclosures and years of hard work. As the owners count the cost of the devastation, another farmer in Scotland recounts her own ordeal - watching her only tractor explode into flames after a petrol bomb attack. With deliberate farm fires on the rise, experts reveal how even a single act of recklessness can cause hundreds of thousands of pounds in damage. And in Hampshire, reporter Paul Colgan meets the innovators using drones to deliver defibrillators to the most remote corners of the countryside. By slashing emergency response times, this cutting-edge technology could transform the chances of survival and save lives on farms and in rural communities across the UK.

programme.title: Lost and Found in the Lakes
programme.desc: The detectorists join forces with the freedivers to find not one but two family heirlooms lost by a heartbroken daughter. Glass artist Peter turns old, thrown-away bottles into stained-glass beauty, and archaeologist Sam looks into what could be our oldest find by our youngest treasure hunter.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: The quiz show where players must avoid Impossible answers to stay in the competition. 20 people start today’s show, but how many of them will survive to face the £10,000 question?

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: The hunt for the nation's Mastermind continues as Clive Myrie tests four more contenders on their specialist subjects and general knowledge under the glare of the spotlight and the ticking clock. The subjects in this episode are Marcus Trescothick, Rupert Brooke, Thomas Cromwell and the films of Wes Anderson.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: Jan has lived in her three-bedroom house for over 30 years, but working seven days a week leaves her little time to clean and organise, and her collection of clothes and shoes are covered in dust. The team has just one day to turn her bedroom into a relaxing sanctuary and give her space to rediscover her love of fashion.

programme.title: If Walls Could Talk
programme.desc: Local colleagues, friends and family members come together to tell the stories of Mossley Mill and how it has endured. From former mill workers, to local anglers and actors, the mill plays host to a wide range of activities, giving people somewhere to belong and cherish.

programme.title: Carl Frampton - On Probation
programme.desc: Carl goes to a unique court in Belfast – one that aims to address the root causes of offending by tackling drug and alcohol issues head on. Carl also meets an old friend taking part in this substance misuse court and finds out if weekly drug tests are helping him stay on track. Carl heads to the north coast, where probation officer Stuart introduces him to a man who has recently been released from Magilligan Prison but has nowhere to live. And a former probationer overcomes her past issues with drugs to accept her university degree, making a pledge to help other people in the same situation.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: The hunt for the nation's Mastermind continues as Clive Myrie tests four more contenders on their specialist subjects and general knowledge under the glare of the spotlight and the ticking clock. The subjects in this episode are Marcus Trescothick, Rupert Brooke, Thomas Cromwell and the films of Wes Anderson.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: Jan has lived in her three-bedroom house for over 30 years, but working seven days a week leaves her little time to clean and organise, and her collection of clothes and shoes are covered in dust. The team has just one day to turn her bedroom into a relaxing sanctuary and give her space to rediscover her love of fashion.

programme.title: The Great British Countryside
programme.desc: Hugh Dennis and Julia Bradbury venture across Britain's biggest county, Yorkshire, from the Moors and the Dales to the coast to discover how Britain's epic past lives on in the most fascinating stories and characters. Hugh takes the controls of a glider, and gets winched down into one of Britain's largest potholes on the end of a rope, past the tallest unbroken waterfall in Britain. Julia finds out how Yorkshire's rocks have turned Agatha Christie's handbag to stone, and how they produce mineral water. For a country the size of Britain, it has the biggest variety of geology on Earth, which has created not only a beautiful landscape, but also a fascinating industrial heritage, a rich history and many legends.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel presents the show in which members of the public are invited to bring along their antiques for examination. This edition from Ramsgate in Kent features two teddy bears with their own x-ray plates from a dentist, a penny with a date which makes it worth a small fortune, a handbag made from an armadillo shell, and a valuable collection of Louis Wain cat pictures.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from the historic Blackpool Tower Circus. Paul Martin is joined by experts Anita Manning and James Lewis. Together the team pick out a selection of interesting antiques and collectibles to be sold at a local auction. James discovers some terracotta tomb figures that could be over 1,000 years old, and Anita gets her hands on a collection of seaside postcards. But the real star of the show is a well-preserved concertina. Paul also takes a look at one of Lancashire's most famous theatres, the Morecambe Winter Gardens, and tries his hand at some watercolour painting with renowned artist Geoff Butterworth.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Nikki Fox, Ruthie Henshall, Danny John-Jules and Ignacio Lopez take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s Belgian rail journey continues in the Dutch speaking region of Flanders. In Antwerp, he discovers the city's historic multibillion-pound diamond industry and drops in at the workshop of an expert. Just outside the city, Michael boards the Dendermonde to Puurs Heritage Railway, run by volunteers, and gets a chance to drive one of its 1950s diesel engines. Heading to Belgium’s third city, Ghent, Michael visits the magnificent cathedral and marvels at a 15th-century Van Eyck masterpiece, the Adoration of the Mystic Lamb, the most stolen painting in the world.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing Simply Provence
programme.desc: It’s fair to say that when it comes to classic national dishes, the French and British like to do things differently. However, both have a passion for poisson. Forty-five per cent of French households eat fish at least once a week, and Marcus wants to find out what kind of fish they like and if there’s a French dish to rival the great British fish and chips. If there's one fruit that might be even more synonymous with Provence than garlic, it's the olive. They’ve been grown here for over 3,500 years, and Marcus wants to understand the region’s passion for these tiny, versatile delights.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham and Michaela Strachan present the latest seasonal wildlife stories live from National Trust Crom, the stunning lakeside reserve cared for by the National Trust. Featuring part one of a special trilogy of short films examining the extraordinary relationship between the reed warbler and the common cuckoo, one of nature’s most fascinating examples of brood parasitism. Meanwhile, Iolo Williams broadcasts live from the Natural History Museum in London, where he turns the spotlight on the capital’s rich and often-overlooked invertebrate life.

programme.title: QI XL
programme.desc: Let Sandi Toksvig bring you to your senses with Aisling Bea, Roisin Conaty, Jessica Fostekew and Alan Davies.

programme.title: If Walls Could Talk
programme.desc: Local colleagues, friends and family members come together to tell the stories of Mossley Mill and how it has endured. From former mill workers, to local anglers and actors, the mill plays host to a wide range of activities, giving people somewhere to belong and cherish.

programme.title: Carl Frampton - On Probation
programme.desc: Carl goes to a unique court in Belfast – one that aims to address the root causes of offending by tackling drug and alcohol issues head on. Carl also meets an old friend taking part in this substance misuse court and finds out if weekly drug tests are helping him stay on track. Carl heads to the north coast, where probation officer Stuart introduces him to a man who has recently been released from Magilligan Prison but has nowhere to live. And a former probationer overcomes her past issues with drugs to accept her university degree, making a pledge to help other people in the same situation.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Matt Chorley.

programme.title: The Road to Hope with Fergal Keane
programme.desc: The BBC’s Fergal Keane has spent 40 years witnessing the worst that humanity can do - genocide, war, and famine. So why is he full of hope? The answer lies in the extraordinary bravery he’s encountered in the worst places. In this powerful and humane film by Oscar-winner Alice Doyard, Fergal argues that despite the anxiety of the present we have real cause for hope.

programme.title: Defiance
programme.desc: Thriller based on a true story. In 1940s eastern Europe, four Jewish brothers flee to the forest to escape persecution and death at the hands of Nazi forces after their parents are murdered. Once there, they find more refugees are using the forest as a hideout, so they band together to share resources and attempt to outwit the German forces, who are always on their tail.

programme.title: Race Across the World
programme.desc: Six months after the race, all five teams reunite to relive their 12,000km journey from Palermo to Mongolia, with unseen moments and unprecedented behind-the-scenes access

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: Springwatch returns for three weeks of seasonal splendour. Broadcasting live from the brand new location of National Trust Crom in Northern Ireland, Chris Packham and Michaela Strachan deliver all the wildlife drama spring has to offer. With remote cameras rigged across the site, they uncover stories unfolding in real time. Iolo Williams undertakes his own wildlife wanderings, broadcasting live from the Knepp Estate in Sussex, where wildlife is thriving and ‘stand-out’ species are returning to the landscape.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: A hundred years ago in Yorkshire, it wasn’t ketchup that people added to their food - it was a delicious locally made relish. By the turn of the 20th century, 30 million bottles of Yorkshire Relish were being made in Leeds each year and shipped around the world. Made of vinegar, sugar, fruits and 27 spices, it was the go-to sauce for generations, right up until the 1950s. In the city where it was made, Danny Sebastian savours a collection of advertising items that celebrate this once-popular condiment. If that doesn’t whet your appetite, enjoy two teams of bargain hunters as they scour the antiques stalls at Wetherby Racecourse. On the red team are twins and classic car fans Mike and Joe, who hope to breakdance their way to victory - as long as they don’t break the bank first! Against them are mum and daughter Sue and Sarah, who plan on using their cha-cha-charm to get a good price. But which team will be dancing all the way to a profit at Caroline Hawley’s auction?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: On the last leg of his journey, Michael Portillo arrives in the historic northern city of Eger. At its famous castle, he discovers how, during the 16th century, Ottoman invaders were defeated by a vastly outnumbered Hungarian force. It‘s a victory still celebrated to this day. Nearby, in the foothills of the Bükk Mountains, one of Hungary’s wine-producing areas, Michael takes a tour of a family-owned vineyard and samples the region’s signature wine, Bull’s Blood. Continuing east, his final destination is the Puszta, Hungary's largest national park, where animals have grazed for over 2,000 years. On a vast plain with endless skies, Michael is treated to an impressive display of horsemanship by Hungarian cowboys, called csikós.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Leicestershire, Brandy, an elderly horse, is trapped in freezing mud on the banks of the Ashby canal. As the exhausted animal weakens, farmers and a specialist fire and rescue team join forces in a race against the clock to save him. With age and size working against him, the team make one final, desperate attempt to bring Brandy to safety, before it’s too late. In Lincolnshire, arson rips through a family farm, destroying buildings, animal enclosures and years of hard work. As the owners count the cost of the devastation, another farmer in Scotland recounts her own ordeal - watching her only tractor explode into flames after a petrol bomb attack. With deliberate farm fires on the rise, experts reveal how even a single act of recklessness can cause hundreds of thousands of pounds in damage. And in Hampshire, reporter Paul Colgan meets the innovators using drones to deliver defibrillators to the most remote corners of the countryside. By slashing emergency response times, this cutting-edge technology could transform the chances of survival and save lives on farms and in rural communities across the UK.

programme.title: Lost and Found in the Lakes
programme.desc: The detectorists join forces with the freedivers to find not one but two family heirlooms lost by a heartbroken daughter. Glass artist Peter turns old, thrown-away bottles into stained-glass beauty, and archaeologist Sam looks into what could be our oldest find by our youngest treasure hunter.

programme.title: Andy's Dino Island
programme.desc: When a Quetzalcoatlus egg Jen has been watching is knocked out of its nest, Andy sets out on an epic adventure across Dino Island to retrieve and reunite it with its family before it hatches. Along the way, a pesky velociraptor steals the egg, and Andy chases after it - right into the path of a sleeping T rex, which soon wakes up!

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle isn’t allowed at school, so he’s being looked after by Connie, the Brooklyn-Bell’s neighbour, at her house. Connie has dressed as a dog and made a huge, doggy maze game from cushions and suitcases for her dog, Jelly, to race through with Waffle. Waffle asks for one more race through the maze at home but Jess explains that the time for noisy play is over and offers him a quiet cuddle instead. After dinner, Evie tells Jess she’s been given her first reading book at school and gets the book out of her school bag to show her Mum. Waffle sits next to Evie and watches her read. When he starts to say words from the book out loud, Evie wonders if he’s reading, but Jess and Simon refuse to believe it.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi, Ruby and Finn play football against Khia’s team. Rafi is goalie, but she keeps missing shots and feels under pressure. She makes a wish for giant hands to save every ball. When the wish ends, Rafi worries she’ll lose, but Ruby and Finn remind her she’s already a great goalie. Believing in herself, Rafi makes a fingertip save on Khia’s penalty and wins the game fairly.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: As JoJo, Gran Gran and 'Team Jared' prepare for the marathon, JoJo begins to worry that she'll be joining Jared on the really long race. Gran Gran lets her know that 'Team Jared' will just be supporting him. JoJo learns that being a supporter is just as important as being a runner.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Sarah and Duck are woken up by a loud clanging overhead and decide to investigate the noise.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: There's going to be a dance fiesta on the Clangers’ planet with a glitterball trophy for the winner. Baby Skymoo really wants to take part, but she is a bit shy and isn't sure if she can dance very well. For the first few dances, Baby Skymoo just watches from the sidelines as Major leads a military twostep, the froglets indulge in some hip hop and Major and Mother excel in a tango. It is only in the final dance, a Viennese waltz, that Baby Skymoo lets go and shows her real dancing talent.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa are having a race, but BaBa always starts before Gramma Leeba says go, never waiting. At Play Time, BaBa knocks down MeMo’s brick tower before it has been built. MeMo and the Yummies encourage BaBa to wait for the snacks to be ready before trying to eat them. BaBa waits - and they're delicious! On the Lullaby Lake, BaBa has learned to wait and is rewarded with a beautiful performance.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: Upsy Daisy, Makka Pakka, the Tombliboos and Igglepiggle go for a ride on the Pinky Ponk. The ball bounces through the garden, what a big bounce! The ball bounces up and hits the Pinky Ponk, sending everyone sliding from one end to the other. Now the Pontipines play with the ball. Look out everybody! The ball hits the Pinky Ponk several times, making it fly in lots of silly ways. What a silly Pinky Ponk!

programme.desc: Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it’s Broccoli and his floret Broc performing their phenomenal ventriloquist act.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Children's animation. Bing has a great time choosing the perfect present for Sula. But when it's time to hand it over, he decides he wants to keep it for himself.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: The children in Tummy Tales play a game of pass the parcel and win a surprise toy, while the Dup Dup delivers toys for the Teletubbies to play with. Even Noo-Noo enjoys a new treat!

programme.title: Tee and Mo
programme.desc: Preschool animation about a baby monkey and his mother. Feeling sad that he can't use his umbrella in the rain, Tee seeks to find out what other uses this mystical item might have.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: It's Harvest Festival in the supermarket, and Supertato tells the Grape Kids, Tomato, Broccoli and Chilli the story of his first Harvest Festival - the day he arrived in the supermarket! But Evil Pea hijacks the story, explaining how she arrived on the same day, and how she and Supertato first met. She reveals a shocking truth - young Supertato helped her freeze all the fruits and veggies in the supermarket! Supertato admits this is true, but there is more to the story.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing and Sula are planting seeds at Amma's when Coco arrives with her new skipping rope. Coco teaches them how to skip, with Sula picking it up quicker than Bing. Just when Bing thinks he has succeeded, he hurts his leg on the watering can! Bing can't understand why he is not as good as Sula, but Coco shows Bing that, with some help, he can learn to skip too!

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: A rockslide blocks Ted the bus and his passengers in a mountain pass. Mojo’s mighty dozer top will make short work of those rocks... if Mojo and Bo can work together!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Mrs Weaver's kits have a question for Duggee. They want to know: what's his favourite badge? Easy - it’s his Squirrel Club badge! The baby worm and the tiny dormouse have questions too. A dot-to-dot reveals Duggee’s head, Tino paints Duggee’s portrait, and Tag builds a car from blocks.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are confused when they see Duggee sitting on a ball because they like to use it differently. Duggee is quick to explain to the Squirrels that there is no right or wrong way to play and that everyone is different. They go on a journey with the ball, watching it bounce, roll and slide from ear to paw as it rebounds between animals. The ball gets hit with a racket, flies through the sky, falls from a cliff and floats in the sea.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Mackenzie, Jack and Rusty are playing astronauts on a mission to Mars!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: At school, Bluey and her friends turn a tree stump into a thrilling helicopter game. But as the pilot, Bluey has to learn to give up some control so they can all have fun.

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: Grandmaster Glitch's digging causes a flood in the Wieliczka Salt Mine. Can the Go Jetters save the famous salt statues?

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Jemima and the ducklings are driven from their coop by Sammy Whiskers, Peter must enlist the unwitting help of Mr McGregor's cat to get her home back.

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: Animated deep sea adventure series. Captain Barnacles and his intrepid band of explorers roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. The Octonauts recruit a shape-shifting mimic octopus to help them recover an important vial of medicinal algae from a moray eel's lair.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: The Numberblocks make a new friend, football fan Eleven, who gets them all in training for the big match. Learn all about the number 11 with Numberblock Eleven!

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. From A to Z, every Alphablock has fun discovering the magic of wordplay. When T gets stuck on top of a mountain, A, E, I, O and U come to the rescue.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: The Piris are in the final of the synchronised swimming competition and are beyond excited. All except Pancake, who worries he will spoil their chances of glory with his two left flippers.

programme.title: Playtime Towers
programme.desc: It’s party time in Playtime Towers, and Bella and Lift enjoy a wibbly-wobbly jelly treat. Over in Boxtropolis, this gives Sketch an idea to paint a jellyfish.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: 'If you do a pretending game you can make your toy do anything you want.' Bing and Sula discover a new toy at Amma's creche - a talking ride-on car. It seems like fun until talkie taxi keeps saying the same thing over and over again. When the taxi crashes and is finally silenced, Bing and Sula use their imagination to play the game they really want to play.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘digger’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. We see lots of different diggers – a driving digger, a dumping digger, a lifting digger and a dizzy digger. There’s a muddy digger, a dozing digger and even a disco digger!

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch
programme.desc: Gus finds his own voice when a talking toy he likes loses its voice.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Kiri and Lou can’t sleep. Pania says she will sing them a song, but only if they stay awake for the whole thing.

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: Ziff, Pipp and Button get creative with empty toilet rolls and turn into Froggie robots.

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are outside a cafe, where they watch a man cleaning the window. Another man sits down at the table with his coffee, only for the window cleaner to drip soapy water into his cup! The two men go inside the cafe to get a new drink, and the Twirlywoos come out to investigate. They each take turns to copy the window cleaner, cleaning first the window, then the table and chair. The Hooter summons them home as the man comes back with a fresh cup of coffee. He sits down, only to find that the Twirlywoos have left the soaking wet sponge on his chair! Back in the boat, Peekaboo is spring cleaning. But when the Twirlywoos return, they have a visit from the Stop-Go Car, who leaves dirty tyre tracks everywhere! Peekaboo rides across the boat on a wave of soapy water, which washes all the muddy marks away.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin meets Jamie at the playing field to try out some different games, and George joins them for a game of boccia. Mr Tumble is feeling sporty too as he gets ready to go swimming. The spotty surprise is a sports day race. Featuring signs for the words running track, swimming and medal.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po follow a trail of flowers that leads them to some very special treasure.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Nigel and Baby Bear welcome babies Jean, Elijah, Noah, Baani, Marta, Evie, and their grown-ups to The Baby Club for a special episode featuring dads and male carers. Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are beach toys which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding baby appropriate beach toys inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The popular song ‘1,2,3,4,5 Once I Caught a Fish Alive’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Baby Bear Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children draw body portraits and learn BSL signs for head, nose and eyes, then sing and sign the action rhyme Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes.

programme.title: What’s in Your Plant Pot?
programme.desc: Chocolate maker Ali shows the Fact Pack a real cacao pod. They discover where chocolate really comes from, how cacao beans change as they are fermented and dried, and how they become tasty chocolate.

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: Rebecca is engrossed in her new book, but Murphi needs feeding. To help deal with his hunger, Rebecca works with him to make tiger bread toast. The Mini Monsters serve up some fantastic dishy animal makes, and Rebecca’s cousin calls with an animal story of his own. None of this excitement is enough to keep Murphi’s tummy quiet. Perhaps the final mega monster make will help – a bottle street.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the Pea-Rexes guide a lively baby Avocadodon back to its herd after it hatches.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: In a game of 'Work', Dad hires Bluey and Bingo at his drainpipe factory. But when Bluey takes charge, Dad finds his new boss pretty tough, especially her no dancing rule.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Norrie admits that she can’t ride her new bike because she finds it too difficult. So Duggee gives her some encouragement and lets her know that there are skills that he is still yet to master too, like skateboarding. In fact, each Squirrel has a skill they find difficult. Tag can’t tie his shoe laces, Happy can’t click his fingers, Roly can’t swing and Betty discovers she can’t blink. Now that she is not alone, Norrie agrees to keep trying as Duggee encourages the Squirrels not to quit when things are difficult and that if at first you don’t succeed, try again! Duggee lets them know that when things are hard, you can always ask for help.

programme.title: Let's Go for a Walk
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers walk through the woods to a place where they can play a spooky game. On the way, they explore the roots of a tree, find a mini waterfall, squelch in the mud and even clean themselves like ducks!

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Magic is in the air as Mum has a wizarding surprise waiting for Iona and Elba in the garden. Later, the whole family head out to launch their kite in the windy sky – but will it take flight?

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Emilio's family are from Cyprus, an island nation in the Mediterranean Sea. Emilio is making two Cypriot recipes for his friends to enjoy. The first is pitta bread! The dough is formed and rolled into ovals and placed on a baking tray. The second is made up of red peppers and his special ingredient, halloumi. They are put onto skewers with an oil, oregano, honey and lemon marinade and put into the oven with his pitta bread. Emilio has made a Cypriot wishing tree for his friends to tie their wishes to. But will they like his recipe when they try it?

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: Maddie heads to a bowling alley to find out how it works. She takes her special cameras and looks behind the lane to see where the pins end up and how they get put back in the right place. We also see underneath the bowling alley to find out how the ball rolls back ready for the player to take another turn. Next Maddie heads to a ribbon factory where they make lots of different types of ribbon from recycled plastic. She uses her special microscope camera to see how the tiny weft and warp yards are woven together to make a tartan ribbon.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: When Dan’s favourite toy goes missing at the Search and Rescue Centre Open Day, Dan needs his super nose to race to the rescue of Squiddy!

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet some brown bears as they eat their breakfast. Using their big claws, they go fishing for fruit. In the wild, these claws help them catch super slippery salmon. Next, they meet a hazel dormouse. This adorable, dinky character has a huge, fluffy tail that he can use like a scarf to wrap around himself to stay warm, but also to balance as he runs through high branches looking for food. These two animals are very different, but Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the unusual and extraordinary wild connection is between them.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle, Simon, Doug, Evie and Ruby do a sponsored silence to raise money for the school. It’s not much fun, so Mrs Hobbs suggests they do a jigsaw. Waffle finds the missing piece.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Chasing rainbows with Oona, Baba, Mossy and May.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: Everyone is bringing presents to the opening of Twinkle’s zen garden, and Yukee wants to take something too. But when she can’t find anything, they encourage her to sing her frustration. Yukee realises that she might have the perfect present after all.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie and Triggs are relaxing in the garden when they hear a meow from next door. It's Phillip's new 'pet' kitten, Peanut! Phillip wants Peanut to do tricks to impress his friends, but Maddie and Triggs help Phillip to understand that there's more to pets than tricks.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee thought his tie was a little bit plain, so he added some accessories and now it looks amazing. The Squirrels admire Duggee’s new look and want to learn how to accessorise themselves. The first step for the Squirrels is to find something they’d like to change. The Squirrels each bring a different item - wellies, a T-shirt, headband, helmet and… a potato. They grab sequins, patches, feathers and lights, and then showcase what they have all done. Norrie has added sequins to her T-shirt and made it into a new wonderfully sparkly outfit. Betty has added loads of useful items to her headband, like a calculator and a pencil, to wear it on all occasions. Roly has painted glow-in-the-dark paint on his wellies, and now he can splash in the dark. Tag has painted his helmet and added horns so he looks super-turbo! Roly has turned his potato into a beautifully made-up face with pink and yellow hair. The Squirrels want to accessorise everything. Soon enough, the whole of the Clubhouse and the town are new and improved, but the Squirrels are getting tired. There’s a chance they may have got carried away, so they go to work toning it down a touch. Less is more!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Numberblock Nine arrives in Numberland, finds a friend in Four, sings a song about squares... and sneezes! Learn all about the number 9 with Numberblock Nine!

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. From A to Z, every Alphablock has fun discovering the magic of wordplay. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog!

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Ben meets friends Thomas and Theodore to do some baking in the kitchen. Mr Tumble is busy getting ready for a celebration, but he has forgotten something important. There is a tea party in this spotty surprise. Featuring signs for the words bowl, invitation and cake.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: The Teletubbies are flamenco dancing! Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po are surprisingly good.

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers discover how acorns play an important role in the environment. They find out how tiny acorns can grow into giant oak trees that live for hundreds of years and that acorns are a great food source for animals like squirrels who bury them to eat in winter. On the way, they spot a woodpecker’s nest in an oak tree and learn that oaks support more life than any other tree in the UK – all thanks to the tiny acorn!

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: Elvis refuses to play football after his lucky, stinky socks are washed. Evie B leads the hunt for the smelliest smell in the Den so they can make the socks stinky again.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: In this flying episode, CBeebies’ very own motorcycle rider, Grace, shows off three amazing machines that are all made to fly! Grace does loop the loops in an aerobatic plane, shows an amazing flying taxi and then heads into the clouds in a hang-glider.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle finds the club’s dressing-up box. Mr Brooklyn-Bell makes use of the costumes for a jungle-themed show, and the box becomes two perfect daybeds for Waffle and George the cat.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Minty tries to fly and is mistaken for a Baby Bokchoydacty by its mother.

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: A shortage of cocoa sends Tunip and the Vegimals to the Amazon.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Tommy Brock decides to move in to the Farmyard, Mittens needs Peter Rabbit's help to evict him!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are out walking around in the rain with Duggee and notice a rainbow! But before they know it, it’s gone and the Squirrels are devastated. They decide to make their own rainbow and go off in search of all the colours from everything around them, including strawberries, carrots and bananas. Duggee shows the Squirrels what he has been working on too - a rainbow cake!

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: When Daphne the giraffe is shy about her diabetes pump, Vida makes a sparkly bag for it!

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: A toy dinosaur rampages through the supermarket and scares the Grape Kids. Carrot and Supertato work out that it’s controlled by a remote control and try to get the dinosaur back in its box.

programme.desc: Spicy directs a show starring Sunny and the eaglets. Weasy wants to join in, but Spicy worries he will overdo it and refuses to give him a role. Weasy forces his way onto the stage, convinced she will recognise his talent.

programme.desc: Mojo and Bo have to deliver a superfun singing valentine. But the problem is, they don’t know who it’s for, or who it’s from. Preston is racing to beat them to it!

programme.title: Millionaire Hot Seat
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson hosts the exciting and fast-paced quiz where each episode sees six hopefuls compete for a one-million-pound prize - however, only one player can take their place in the Hot Seat at a time and answer multiple-choice questions to work their way up the Money Ladder. Unlike classic Millionaire, each question is against the clock and there is no room for indecision - if a player answers correctly, they remain in the Hot Seat and continue up the Money Ladder, but if they get a question wrong, they are eliminated, the Top Prize drops down, and the next player takes their place. Each player is given one Pass - a chance to pass the question on to the next player - but in doing so forfeit their place in the Hot Seat and risk not making it back there later on. Only one player will have a chance to win the top prize remaining on the ladder, and the player taking on that question must answer it correctly to take home the cash.

programme.title: The Vardys
programme.desc: At Jamie's final game for Leicester City, he scores his 200th goal for the club - it's a fairytale ending to one of the greatest underdog stories in sporting history. But he's not done with football yet, and the search for his new club begins. As speculation mounts, the Vardys consider offers from clubs all wanting to sign the 38-year-old striker. But none are in England, which forces the family to consider: would they go with Jamie, or stay at home? On deadline day, there is last-minute chaos as Jamie decides between two top clubs, one in Holland and the other in Italy. At the eleventh hour, he takes the Italian job. The Vardys are going to Italy! Determined to stay together as a family unit, Becky flies to Italy to find a house and schools for the kids - but in rainy Milan, nothing goes to plan.

programme.title: Torvill & Dean: The Last Dance
programme.desc: Jayne Torvill and Christopher Dean reflect candidly on a remarkable 50-year career on ice as this fly-on-the-wall documentary captures every moment throughout their final UK and Australia tour and the prospect of an emotional 'Last Dance' - our cameras follow the Olympic legends behind-the-scenes throughout their final year as performers, from their preparations and final television performance on Dancing on Ice to the early gruelling training sessions and first rehearsals in Scotland, the iconic first show of the live tour in London, and then throughout the next energy-sapping four months as the duo tour with the support of an ensemble cast of world-class skaters, a unique show that tells their life story from their first meeting to their final-ever performance. There is every chance the wheels may come off, and this film captures the raw emotion of life on the road.

programme.title: Torvill & Dean: The Last Dance

programme.title: Millionaire Hot Seat
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson hosts the exciting and fast-paced quiz where each episode sees six hopefuls compete for a one-million-pound prize - however, only one player can take their place in the Hot Seat at a time and answer multiple-choice questions to work their way up the Money Ladder. Unlike classic Millionaire, each question is against the clock and there is no room for indecision - if a player answers correctly, they remain in the Hot Seat and continue up the Money Ladder, but if they get a question wrong, they are eliminated, the Top Prize drops down, and the next player takes their place. Each player is given one Pass - a chance to pass the question on to the next player - but in doing so forfeit their place in the Hot Seat and risk not making it back there later on. Only one player will have a chance to win the top prize remaining on the ladder, and the player taking on that question must answer it correctly to take home the cash.

programme.title: The Vardys
programme.desc: At Jamie's final game for Leicester City, he scores his 200th goal for the club - it's a fairytale ending to one of the greatest underdog stories in sporting history. But he's not done with football yet, and the search for his new club begins. As speculation mounts, the Vardys consider offers from clubs all wanting to sign the 38-year-old striker. But none are in England, which forces the family to consider: would they go with Jamie, or stay at home? On deadline day, there is last-minute chaos as Jamie decides between two top clubs, one in Holland and the other in Italy. At the eleventh hour, he takes the Italian job. The Vardys are going to Italy! Determined to stay together as a family unit, Becky flies to Italy to find a house and schools for the kids - but in rainy Milan, nothing goes to plan.

programme.title: Torvill & Dean: The Last Dance
programme.desc: Jayne Torvill and Christopher Dean reflect candidly on a remarkable 50-year career on ice as this fly-on-the-wall documentary captures every moment throughout their final UK and Australia tour and the prospect of an emotional 'Last Dance' - our cameras follow the Olympic legends behind-the-scenes throughout their final year as performers, from their preparations and final television performance on Dancing on Ice to the early gruelling training sessions and first rehearsals in Scotland, the iconic first show of the live tour in London, and then throughout the next energy-sapping four months as the duo tour with the support of an ensemble cast of world-class skaters, a unique show that tells their life story from their first meeting to their final-ever performance. There is every chance the wheels may come off, and this film captures the raw emotion of life on the road.

programme.title: Millionaire Hot Seat
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson hosts the exciting and fast-paced quiz where each episode sees six hopefuls compete for a one-million-pound prize - however, only one player can take their place in the Hot Seat at a time and answer multiple-choice questions to work their way up the Money Ladder. Unlike classic Millionaire, each question is against the clock and there is no room for indecision - if a player answers correctly, they remain in the Hot Seat and continue up the Money Ladder, but if they get a question wrong, they are eliminated, the Top Prize drops down, and the next player takes their place. Each player is given one Pass - a chance to pass the question on to the next player - but in doing so forfeit their place in the Hot Seat and risk not making it back there later on. Only one player will have a chance to win the top prize remaining on the ladder, and the player taking on that question must answer it correctly to take home the cash.

programme.title: The Vardys
programme.desc: At Jamie's final game for Leicester City, he scores his 200th goal for the club - it's a fairytale ending to one of the greatest underdog stories in sporting history. But he's not done with football yet, and the search for his new club begins. As speculation mounts, the Vardys consider offers from clubs all wanting to sign the 38-year-old striker. But none are in England, which forces the family to consider: would they go with Jamie, or stay at home? On deadline day, there is last-minute chaos as Jamie decides between two top clubs, one in Holland and the other in Italy. At the eleventh hour, he takes the Italian job. The Vardys are going to Italy! Determined to stay together as a family unit, Becky flies to Italy to find a house and schools for the kids - but in rainy Milan, nothing goes to plan.
